title: Replica crosstalk emulation and ordering probe
content:
Status: working notes / reproducible experiment plan

SUMMARY
This is an exploratory log for an experiment that intentionally injects cross-replica "crosstalk" (transient neighbor noise, packet reordering and NCCL op interleaving) to observe ordering sensitivity in pipeline/tensor parallel LLM inference. Goal: surface subtle tail-latency failure modes that don't show up in pure synthetic allreduce microbenchmarks.

Motivation / why this matters
- Production inference uses heterogeneous concurrent workloads: small chat requests, long contexts, kv-cache hits/misses. Replica-level interference (host NIC bursts, scheduling jitter, ordering differences between NCCL collectives) can create rare but high-impact tail spikes.
- We suspect that some tail events previously attributed to "link saturation" are actually from NCCL op order inversion + replica scheduling skew. If true, mitigations are different (ordering-stable collective sequencing, backpressure at request demux, lightweight gateway fencing).

Hypotheses
1) Reordering a subset of allreduce/recv operations across replicas leads to transient KV-cache replay and extra host staging, creating 1-3x tail latency multipliers for short requests.
2) Small bursts on the host NIC (1-5ms) timed to happen during tile barrier points cause NCCL to change fallback to p2p for certain messages and produce >99.99th spikes.
3) Deterministic NCCL ordering (pinning op sequence + epoch tagging) reduces these rare spikes but may increase median latency slightly due to stricter sync. Tradeoff worth measuring.

Testbed and baseline config
- Cluster: 4x nodes, each 8x A100 (40GB) in DGX-ish interconnect topology (NVLink mesh inside node, 100GbE/IB between nodes).
- Serving runtime: local branch replicate-order-probe (wip) with logging hooks on NCCL op start/complete, and a short capture mode (structured log lines).
- Models: llama-2-13b-chat-like sharded across 4 GPUs (TP+PP hybrid: tp=2, pp=2). Sequence lengths: short (64), medium (512), long (2048) to exercise kv-cache and reshape.
- Workloads: mix of 80% short chat, 15% medium, 5% long. QPS set so average GPU utilization ~65%.

Tools used / injection mechanisms
- tc netem + ifb on host to add small spike delay (10ms) and reorder (netem 'delay' + 'reorder' knobs) targeted at specific dst ports used by NCCL verbs proxies.
- custom injector that pauses the process on certain PIDs for 1-3ms windows aligned with NCCL collective timestamps (we instrument the runtime to emit a short banner when reaching collective barrier). This is coarse but reproducible in controlled runs.
- bpftrace probes to capture kernel NIC queue drops and precise timestamping of send/recv syscalls.
- NCCL debug env (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO) captured and filtered; we correlate op ids and sizes to observe fallback decisions.

Experiment matrix (first pass)
1) Baseline (no injection) — 30m run to capture steady-state and tail.
2) Netem burst injection on 1 node, randomized 1ms-10ms spikes every 500ms — observe tail.
3) Process pause injection aligned to collective start on a single rank — tight worst-case probe.
4) Deterministic ordering patch enabled (runtime enforces per-step op ordering across replicas using a cheap token exchange) + repeat injections.
Each run: 30m, warmup 5m, collect: per-request latency histogram, NCCL op logs, kernel NIC timestamps, per-GPU PCIe host staging counts.

Key observations (early, from a handful of runs)
- Baseline: 99.9th latency ~ 85ms for short requests.
- Netem bursts: occasional 99.99th spikes up to 1.1s. Spikes correlate with a cluster of small NCCL 'recv' ops (<=4KB) switching from NVLink to p2p fallback path — likely because of transient link timeout that caused the ring to reconfigure.
- Process pause at collective start: deterministic recreation of 400–700ms spike on the target replica; other replicas showed delayed responses due to retry/backoff behavior in the runtime.
- Ordering patch: reduced number of >300ms events by ~60% in these tests, but median latency rose ~4ms (likely from extra handshake per step).

Detailed micro-findings
- KV-cache replay: When a fast path expects a KV slot but the replica was delayed during the KV-cache feed op, the runtime falls back to a host-side replay which queues an extra synchronous RPC to the host, adding ~40–70ms per event. This shows up as a tight cluster in the trace where recv sizes are small but latency jumps.
- NCCL op IDs: we observed op ID sequences being interleaved in two distinct orders across runs when bursts occur. This points to reorder-by-arrival semantics in the low-level transport layer.
- PCIe staging amplification: small inter-replica delays increase rate of host-to-device copies due to additional cache misses; on node with bursts, GPU PCIe queue depth peaked and GPU-side stalls increased.

Quick wins / mitigations to prototype
- Add a tiny leader-based step token (1 byte handshake) before critical KV-cache collectives to enforce sequence (cheap, reduces ordering variance).
- Soft backpressure at request demux: if frontier per-replica latency > threshold, throttle short requests routing to that replica until it recovers.
- Adaptive NCCL fallback tuning: increase threshold for fallback to p2p for very small messages to avoid oscillation on transient jitter.

Metrics to collect for final paper/PR
- Per-run histograms: p50/p90/p99/p99.9/p99.99 for short/medium/long with and without mitigations.
- NCCL op timeline aligned with per-request timeline; heatmap of op-size vs latency spike probability.
- Host NIC queue occupation vs spike incidence.
- Count of KV-cache replays and extra host-staging calls per hour.

Open questions / unknowns
- How much of the observed ordering inversion is driven by RDMA hardware vs. libfabric-layer queuing? Need capture at NIC firmware level (vendor trace) to be sure.
- What's the cost of deterministic ordering at 100% load? We saw median grow slightly in low-load tests; need stress runs at 90–95% GPU util.
- Is a leader token sufficient for heterogeneous model shards (different sizes of collectives)? Some collectives are hundreds of KB — token handshake cost negligible, but sequencing may cause head-of-line effects.

Next steps (actionable)
- Run full 6-hour matrix across tp/pp variants (tp=1,2,4; pp=1,2) with injection scenarios to measure combinatorial sensitivity (assigned to Marco).
- Prototype leader-token patch in a fork and run at 80% and 95% util with extra telemetry enabled (assigned to Janelle).
- File a vendor support case for NIC-level trace access and see if vendor can show reorder logs (assigned to Diego).

Notes to self / loose thoughts
- This feels like a scheduling + ordering issue rather than pure bandwidth. That changes mitigation approach (software sequencing vs hardware scaling).
- Keep an eye on how mitigation interacts with batching heuristics — ordering can inhibit batch fusion if implemented naively.
- Consider a lightweight probabilistic fencing: only enforce strict ordering for "kv-cache critical" collectives identified by op-size and request type.

References / links
- quick perf harness: github PR (see linked_artifacts).
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime: "replica-crosstalk" (internal link)

If reviewer wants a reproducible run recipe, I can dump the exact tc/netem commands and the tracer startup sequence in the next revision.
